dialect.detail: Likely GnuCOBOL or similar COBOL-85+ compiler supporting nested programs, GLOBAL data items, and qualified data-name references. The nested program structure with END PROGRAM markers and GLOBAL clause are COBOL-85 features.
evidence: Nested programs with END PROGRAM markers
CALL PGM3 OF JKL and CALL PGM3 OF GHI OF DEF OF ABC (qualified data-name in CALL)
Multiple PROGRAM-ID entries in single file

purpose.domain_detail: Compiler/runtime test for nested program scoping, GLOBAL data visibility, qualified data-name references in CALL statements, and condition-name (88-level) usage in CALL targets
purpose.summary: A test program (test9014) containing multiple nested subprograms (test9014a, test9014a1, test9014a2, test9014b, test9014b1, test9014b2) that exercise COBOL nested program features including GLOBAL data sharing, qualified data-name references in CALL statements, and 88-level condition names used as CALL targets. The file appears to be part of a compiler or runtime test suite validating scoping rules.

notable_features: Nested programs with END PROGRAM delimiters
Qualified data-name references in CALL (e.g., CALL PGM3 OF JKL)
88-level condition names used as CALL targets via SET ... TO TRUE
Multiple SELECT/ASSIGN entries with various assign formats (UT-S-, S-, bare, literal)
No PERFORM statements - all control flow via CALL and EXIT PROGRAM
verdict.notes: The file is clearly a test suite program designed to exercise nested program scoping and GLOBAL data visibility rules. The assign names include nonsense words (BEEP, ABORT, ASCII, EBCDIC, MAGIC, CLAMBAKE, ASCDIC, EBCII, BLURN, BLERGH) suggesting deliberate test data rather than production code. No comments present. The qualified CALL targets (CALL PGM3 OF JKL) are unusual and likely testing a specific compiler feature.
